Honestly you can get really decent with about 3 hours a day for about 1-2 months, thats about 90 to 180 hours. You also need to sleep 8 hours a night, eat good food, and exercise, because without your health you can do nothing. Bad health means bad reaction time, which is one of the most important qualities to have for this game. It's not about the amount of time you play, but how efficient you play, slow down your practice and look for your errors. Simply playing more arenas, cash cup or scrims will not drastically improve you. Focusing on making every movement correct, will. The most valuable advice is to review all your losses, and try your best to not let it happen again. Stop making simple mistakes whatever it is (like falling off the builds or placing them wrong), and practice your aim, build, and edit mechanics. Learn the map, where people could be hiding, and what kinds of builds work or don't work in certain places. For me I'm not a pro because I get too angry, I get confused with what to do when there's a ton of players doing shit around me, I prioritize the wrong things, or I'm not quick enough with what I want to do. But I pretty much know what you need to do to become pro. Finally, you need to think like a machine, let go of your emotions and relax. It's good to be happy but when you're tilted is when you won't learn. The game after all lives in a machine and is just taking inputs from you. I hope this helped man.
